messages:
Aisha (Support): Heads up — Enterprise customer 'BrightEdge' just flagged missing audit events for a 3-hour window yesterday (approx 02:10–05:10 UTC). They say they need the logs for compliance. :alarm_clock:
Marcus (SRE): Ack. Any repro artifacts from the customer? about which API routes / keys?
Aisha (Support): They supplied a sample request id: `req_8f3a2b`. Also pasted a snippet from their SIEM showing `403` spikes and then no audit entries after 02:12.
Marta (Account Exec): They're asking if this is related to the KMS rotation we did last week. Customer is worried about scope and whether to notify their auditors.
Lena (Security): Noted — we need to verify whether HSM/KMS operations could have impacted audit emission or just access checks. Marcus, can you check proxy logs + audit pipeline for `req_8f3a2b`?
Marcus (SRE): Starting trace. Quick check: our audit ingestion shows a short processing backlog at 02:09–02:14 (consumer lag ~7m) but messages were processed. I'm pulling raw Kafka partition range now.
ops-bot: deploy-digest: rotation-worker v2.14 deployed 2025-11-07T01:43:10Z (no errors).
Tom (Platform Eng): The KMS rotation finished at 01:30 UTC last week, unrelated time. But there was a transient auth cache refresh job around 02:05 UTC yesterday on the EU cluster — might be correlated.
Aisha (Support): Customer also reported auth errors earlier (`AuthError: key not found`) — they pasted this in thread. Could be auth caching mismatch.
Lena (Security): Two action items: (1) confirm whether missing audit entries are ingestion drop vs never-emitted from runtime; (2) scope: list customers with requests hitting the same node group/time window. If KMS/HSM touched keys, escalate.
Marcus (SRE): Evidence so far: runtime produced logs for `req_8f3a2b` (stdout) but the audit-pusher returned 504 for a 2m interval due to upstream timeout. I have the nginx proxy snippet: ```
[02:11:22] "POST /v1/generate" 200 124ms
[02:11:22] audit-pusher -> 504 gateway timeout (retry)
[02:12:50] audit-pusher -> 200 ok
```
Tom (Platform Eng): That matches a short outage on audit-ingest service — scaling decision delayed. Not a KMS issue.
Marta (Account Exec): Customer wants a timeline and whether they need to self-notify. What's our recommended comms?
Lena (Security): If this is an ingestion processing gap (audit-pusher upstream timeout) and we can restore full logs for the window from the runtime logs/kafka replay, then we can provide the missing entries and a mitigation note. If not, we must treat it as 'gap' and advise customer per our retention/audit policy. Need ETA on recovery.
Marcus (SRE): ETA: raw runtime logs available for replay within 45m. Kafka replay to audit-store to fill missing range likely ~2h once I start the backfill. I'll confirm if any messages were permanently dropped (shouldn't be).
Aisha (Support): I'll draft initial customer message: short explanation + ETA for backfill and offer to share exported evidence. Want security to approve wording.
Lena (Security): Share draft here. Include: what happened, scope (list of affected projects if known), root cause (audit-pusher transient timeout), remediation (replay + extra monitoring), and whether KMS/HSM was involved (no evidence at this time).
Aisha (Support): Draft -> "We identified a brief processing outage in our audit ingestion pipeline on <date> that caused a delay in storing some audit events for ~2–7 minutes. We are replaying runtime logs and expect to restore the missing entries within ~2 hours. There is no indication that KMS/HSM rotations or key material were involved. We'll follow up when replay completes and provide an export suitable for your compliance review." Thoughts?
Tom (Platform Eng): Good. Add that we're adding a guardrail to reject requests on audit-pusher 5xxs starting next week to avoid silent gaps.
Marta (Account Exec): Customer reply: thanks — they want an official timeline and a confirmation if any data was lost.
Lena (Security): If backfill succeeds, confirm no data loss. If backfill fails for any partition, escalate to legal/compliance for notification thresholds. Keep me in the loop.
Marcus (SRE): I'm kicking off the backfill now. I'll post progress updates here.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: backfill job `bf-2049-11-23-01` started by Marcus at 2049990045.
Marcus (SRE): Update: 50% partitions replayed, no dropped messages so far. Estimated 60 more minutes.
Aisha (Support): Notifying customer with the approved draft + we say we'll update in 60–90m. Sending now. :email:
